original_question: Let (T (t))t≥0 be a not necessary strongly continuous semigroup on a Banach space X and consider the following condition. (i) (0, ∞) ∋ t 7→ T (t) ∈ L(X) is analytic. (ii) t 7→ T (t) is analytic on a sector containing R+ (iii) kT (t)k ≤ Metω , dtd T (t) ∈ L(X) and k dtd T (t)k ≤ Mt etω for some constants ω, M. Under which assumption added to (i), (ii) or (iii) does there exist a sectorial operator A generating (T (t))t≥0 ?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 5: "Existence of a generator for analytic semigroups."
correct_elements: Your draft already targets the correct open problem in the paper: a semigroup on a Banach space that is not assumed strongly continuous, three candidate analyticity/differentiability hypotheses (i)–(iii), and the question of when these imply the existence of a sectorial generator for the semigroup. The overall scope and intent are very close to the paper.
missing_details: The semigroup structure should be stated explicitly: (T(t))_{t\ge 0} \subseteq L(X) with T(0)=I and T(t+s)=T(t)T(s) for all s,t\ge 0.
In (i), the analyticity is operator-valued: the map (0,\infty) \to L(X), t \mapsto T(t), is analytic.
In (ii), the analyticity is complex analyticity of an L(X)-valued extension to a sector in \mathbb{C} containing \mathbb{R}_+.
In (iii), the derivative is taken for t>0, as an L(X)-valued derivative.
The exact estimate in (iii) is \|T'(t)\| \le (M/t)e^{\omega t}; the draft formula is ambiguous and misses the 1/t factor.
The constants M and \omega are fixed constants, and the bounds in (iii) are meant to hold for all t>0.
The paper asks what extra assumption must be added to one of (i), (ii), or (iii), not necessarily to all three at once.
The conclusion should specify that the desired operator is a sectorial operator A on X generating the given semigroup (T(t))_{t\ge 0} in the usual semigroup-theoretic sense.
The paper presents this as an open problem, not as a proved theorem or conjecture with a stated answer.
refined_question: Let X be a Banach space and let (T(t))_{t\ge 0}\subseteq L(X) be a semigroup, not assumed to be strongly continuous. Assume that one of the following holds: (i) the operator-valued map (0,\infty)\to L(X), t\mapsto T(t), is analytic; (ii) t\mapsto T(t) extends to an analytic L(X)-valued map on a sector of \mathbb{C} containing \mathbb{R}_+; or (iii) there exist constants M>0 and \omega\in\mathbb{R} such that \|T(t)\|\le Me^{\omega t} for all t>0, the derivative T'(t)=\frac{d}{dt}T(t) exists in L(X) for all t>0, and \|T'(t)\|\le \frac{M}{t}e^{\omega t} for all t>0. What additional assumption(s), when added to one of (i)–(iii), guarantee the existence of a sectorial operator A on X that generates the semigroup (T(t))_{t\ge 0}?
justification: The draft is a near-verbatim restatement of the paper's Section 1, Problem 5, whose title is exactly "Existence of a generator for analytic semigroups." The paper does not give a narrower reformulation nearby, nor an equivalent theorem that should replace it; it simply records the open problem and its source. The only substantive repairs needed are to make the semigroup axioms explicit, clarify that (i) and (ii) concern L(X)-valued analyticity, and correct the line-broken estimate in (iii) to the standard \|T'(t)\|\le (M/t)e^{\omega t} form visible in the underlying Bari/OPSO source that the paper reproduces.
